name: Sunn Hemp
harvestProduct: green manure / biomass mulch (terminated before or at flowering)

evidence.quote: Suited to the warm summer rainfall areas (or irrigation). Plant as soon as soil temperatures are higher than 16°C (October – November)
evidence.doc: Black | Sunn Hemp product page, Barenbrug South Africa

evidence.quote: Plant as soon as soil temperatures are higher than 16°C (October – November)
evidence.doc: Black | Sunn Hemp product page, Barenbrug South Africa

evidence.quote: This is a tropical legume that has huge potential as a cover crop. It is planted in the warm season and is an annual that produces large quantities of biomass.
evidence.doc: Conservation Agriculture Manual, Chapter 5: Cover crops, Grain SA, 2016

evidence.quote: It has been used extensively as a soil improvement or green manure crop in the tropics because of its ability to produce large amounts of biomass in as little as 60 to 90 days.
evidence.doc: Black | Sunn Hemp product page, Barenbrug South Africa

daysToHarvestRange.notes: Days to reach a large-biomass state for termination as green manure, not a fixed flowering date; no SA source gives days-to-flower specifically.

Red | Sunn Hemp product page, Barenbrug South Africa

evidence.quote: It has a suppression effect on plant parasitic nematodes and fixes around 120kg/ha of nitrogen.
evidence.doc: Conservation Agriculture Manual, Chapter 5: Cover crops, Grain SA, 2016

varieties.name: Black Sunn Hemp
varieties.note: High fibre content, more difficult to manage as a green manure; fast establishment, short growing season.

evidence.quote: High fibre content making it more difficult to manage as a green manure
evidence.doc: Black | Sunn Hemp product page, Barenbrug South Africa

varieties.name: Red Sunn Hemp
varieties.note: Low in fibre, fast deterioration as a green manure; medium-fast establishment, long growing season.

evidence.quote: Low in fibre, fast deterioration as a green manure
evidence.doc: Red | Sunn Hemp product page, Barenbrug South Africa

zoneNotes.western-cape: No source evidence found for sunn hemp in winter-rainfall areas; it is a warm-season legume needing soil temp above 16°C.

gaps: Row/in-row spacing not found in any SA source (Barenbrug gives only a broadcast/drilled seeding rate).
Dry-matter biomass t/ha not found for sunn hemp specifically (only N-fixed figure).
sowMonths for all-year/mild-frost zones inferred from a generic 'warm summer rainfall areas' description, not zone-specific confirmation.
summary: Well sourced for sow window (Oct-Nov, soil temp >16°C), seed rate (20-50 kg/ha, cultivar dependent) and N-fixation (~120 kg/ha, Grain SA CA manual). Row/in-row spacing and a dry-matter biomass or yield figure are not sourced in any acceptable SA document and are recorded as gaps.
